name: Making sure AI systems are fair to everyone
gist: These papers address bias in AI—ensuring models don't unfairly discriminate against groups of people and that decisions are explainable and legitimate to everyone affected.
explain: A credit scoring model is trained on historical loan data. Historically, banks discriminated against certain groups, so the data is biased: those groups had fewer approvals and higher default rates (partly because they were steered into worse terms, partly because of economic inequality). A model trained on this data learns those patterns and replicates the discrimination. A hiring model trained on resumes and hiring decisions will learn the historical biases of the hiring committee. A language model trained on internet text will absorb stereotypes and slurs. This is algorithmic bias: the model doesn't intend to discriminate, but it learned discrimination from data. And because the model is faster and cheaper than human review, it can scale the harm to millions of people. Worse, it can hide behind a veneer of objectivity: 'the model said so' sounds more authoritative than 'I think so.'

Why is this hard? Because bias in data is often invisible at first. You might not notice that your training set has fewer examples of women in engineering, or that it has stereotypical descriptions of certain ethnic groups. And even if you notice, it's not obvious how to fix it. If you remove features (like race or gender), the model can often recreate the discrimination using correlated features—zip code, education level, name. And fairness itself is contested: there are multiple incompatible definitions of fairness, and satisfying one often breaks others. For example, if you define fairness as equal accuracy across groups, but one group's data is less representative, then you might have to degrade the model's overall accuracy. If you define fairness as equal approval rates, you might approve people who will default. There is no free lunch.

The papers in this area work on detection, measurement, and mitigation. Detection includes audits and tests that reveal whether a model discriminates. Measurement means defining fairness precisely—there are dozens of definitions, each capturing something different. Mitigation includes re-weighting training data to balance it across groups, using fairness constraints during training, applying post-hoc thresholding to balance outcomes, or using causal reasoning to understand which discrimination is justified (someone's credit score correlates with income, which is a real predictor) and which is not (same score but different approval based on race). Some papers also study explainability: if a model makes a decision about you, you should be able to understand why. A decision that is fair in aggregate might still harm specific individuals, so some work focuses on fairness for individuals. And some papers study the human side: how do people perceive and trust algorithmic decisions, and what does fairness mean to them?

papers.title: Bias Similarity Measurement: A Black-Box Audit of Fairness Across LLMs
papers.contribution: Reveals that instruction tuning enforces abstention rather than altering internal representations; family signatures diverge with Gemma favoring refusal, LLaMA 3.1 approaching neutrality; Gemma 3 Instruct matches GPT-4 fairness at far lower cost.

papers.title: BiasFreeBench: a Benchmark for Mitigating Bias in Large Language Model Responses
papers.contribution: Establishes first unified testbed for bias mitigation research, systematically comparing prompting vs. training paradigms, model sizes, and generalization across key dimensions.

papers.title: Doubly-Regressing Approach for Subgroup Fairness
papers.contribution: Outperforms baseline methods especially when the number of sensitive attributes is large, with much less computation than directly reducing supIPM.

papers.title: Fair Classification by Direct Intervention on Operating Characteristics
papers.contribution: Simultaneously satisfies approximate demographic parity, equalized odds, and predictive parity on COMPAS and ACSIncome with few interventions and minimal accuracy loss.

papers.title: Fair Conformal Classification via Learning Representation-Based Groups
papers.contribution: Approach achieves compact prediction sets with adaptive equalized coverage across unfairly treated subgroups.

papers.title: Fair Policy Aggregation from Standard Policy Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive fairness guarantees to prior work while being orders of magnitude more efficient in computation and demonstrates efficient use of policy optimization.

papers.title: Fair in Mind, Fair in Action? A Synchronous Benchmark for Understanding and Generation in UMLLMs
papers.contribution: Uncovers systemic phenomena like generation gap, personality splits, and counter-stereotype reward while offering diagnostics to guide UMLMM fairness optimization, resolving fairness metric conflicts.

papers.title: Fairness via Independence: A General Regularization Framework for Machine Learning
papers.contribution: CS Divergence provides tighter theoretical bounds than alternative measures, unifying prior fairness efforts under a consistent principle.

papers.title: From Gradient Volume to Shapley Fairness: Towards Fair Multi-Task Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across diverse supervised and reinforcement learning benchmarks with controllable complexity.

papers.title: Multi-Feature Quantized Self-Attention for Fair Large Language Models
papers.contribution: MQAR consistently reduces bias across multiple protected attributes on five LLMs (BERT, T5, GPT-Neo, Mixtral, LLaMA 3.2) while maintaining downstream accuracy within 0.4% of baseline.

papers.title: Person-Centric Annotations of LAION-400M: Auditing Bias and Its Transfer to Models
papers.contribution: Uncover demographic imbalances and harmful associations, showing 60-70% of gender bias in CLIP and Stable Diffusion traces to data co-occurrences.

papers.title: A Causal Decomposition Approach for Fair Contextual Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.contribution: Achieves sublinear regret and violation bounds without Slater's condition, with O(1) per-round complexity for logistic bandits using online mirror descent.

papers.title: A Fair Bayesian Inference through Matched Gibbs Posterior
papers.contribution: Outperforms other methods in balancing uncertainty-fairness and utility-fairness trade-offs while offering efficient MCMC computation.

papers.title: A Game-Theoretic Framework for Measuring and Explaining Metric Compatibility in Fair Machine Learning
papers.contribution: Reveals fairness and utility are often structurally orthogonal rather than conflicting; debiasing improves fairness by compressing compatibility space.

papers.title: A General Framework for Fair and Robust Regression
papers.contribution: Shows clear improvements over existing fair regression in both robustness and predictive performance across simulations and real data.

papers.title: Adaptive Logit Adjustment for Debiasing Multimodal Language Models
papers.contribution: Effectively mitigates bias in image captioning and VQA tasks while maintaining contextual accuracy and demonstrates model-agnostic applicability across VLMs and LMMs.

papers.title: Automatically Finding Reward Model Biases
papers.contribution: Automatically finds reward model biases including novel ones (e.g., redundant spacing and hallucinated content) in leading models like Skywork-V2-8B, with evolutionary iteration outperforming flat search and validation on synthetic biases.

papers.title: Beyond Procedure: Substantive Fairness in Conformal Prediction
papers.contribution: Equalized set sizes, rather than coverage, strongly correlate with improved substantive fairness in conformal prediction systems.

papers.title: Bi-directional Bias Attribution: Debiasing Large Language Models without Modifying Prompts
papers.contribution: Method effectively reduces bias while preserving overall model performance across three widely used LLMs without prompt modification.

papers.title: BiasBusters: Uncovering and Mitigating Tool Selection Bias in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Identifies unfairness as critical deployment obstacle and demonstrates that text-based safety alignment partially transfers to multimodal domains.

papers.title: Bridging Fairness and Explainability: Can Input-Based Explanations Promote Fairness in Hate Speech Detection?
papers.contribution: Shows explanations effectively detect biased predictions and supervise training but unreliably select fair models, bridging explainability and fairness in NLP.

papers.title: COFT: Counterfactual–Conformal Decoding for Fair Chain‑of‑Thought Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reduces bias metrics by 30-55% (median 38%) while preserving task utility, language quality, and reasoning accuracy with <11% computational overhead.

papers.title: COPF: An Online Framework for Deployment-Stable Counterfactual Fairness in Evolving Graphs
papers.contribution: Reduces worst-case spikes in exposure-counterfactual disparities with modest ranking impact; includes residual outcome indistinguishability bounds under temporal mixing.

papers.title: Causal Disentangled Anchor Learning for Scalable Fair Multi-view Clustering
papers.contribution: CDAL proves identifiability of disentangled factors and guarantees linear time complexity O(n), achieving superior utility-fairness trade-offs on large-scale benchmarks.

papers.title: Correcting Overparameterization Effects in Fair Empirical Risk Minimization
papers.contribution: Provides actionable analysis of fair ERM in overparameterized regimes and an estimable search interval for required overcompensation levels.

papers.title: Demystifying the Optimal Fair Classifier in Multi-Class Classification
papers.contribution: Both methods converge to the optimal accuracy-fairness Pareto frontier and demonstrate superior performance in balancing accuracy and fairness on multiple datasets.

papers.title: Desirable Effort Fairness and Optimality Trade-offs in Strategic Learning
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees on the principal's optimality loss under desirability fairness constraints for multiple fairness measures and demonstrates explicit tradeoffs via experiments on real datasets.

papers.title: Differentiable Optimization Layers for Guaranteed Fairness in Deep Learning
papers.contribution: Fairness layer provides provable aggregate fairness guarantees and differentiability properties during backpropagation, validated through numerical experiments.

papers.title: Emergence of Hierarchical Emotion Organization in Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals that larger models develop more complex emotion hierarchies and uncovers systematic biases in emotion recognition across socioeconomic personas.

papers.title: Equalized Generative Treatment: Matching f-divergences for Fairness in Generative Models
papers.contribution: Min-max methods consistently achieve fairer outcomes than other approaches while maintaining competitive overall performance on image and text generation tasks.

papers.title: Extending Fair Null-Space Projections for Continuous Attributes to Kernel Methods
papers.contribution: Theoretically derives kernel-based fairness projection applicable to continuous protected attributes with competitive performance against contemporary methods.

papers.title: Fair Classification with Efficient and Post-hoc Controllable Fairness-Accuracy Trade-off
papers.contribution: Achieves trade-off efficiency comparable to or exceeding in-processing methods without requiring any retraining.

papers.title: Fair Decision Utility in Human-AI Collaboration: Interpretable Confidence Adjustment for Humans with Cognitive Disparities
papers.contribution: Establishes interpretable fairness-aware objective for AI confidence adjustment; demonstrates through theoretical and empirical analysis that utility fairness requires both human-alignment and inter-group-alignment.

papers.title: Fair Decisions from Calibrated Scores: Achieving Optimal Classification While Satisfying Sufficiency
papers.contribution: Simple post-processing algorithm attains optimal classifier and identifies when minimizing separation deviation subject to sufficiency is achievable.

papers.title: Fair Graph Machine Learning under Adversarial Missingness Processes
papers.contribution: BFtS achieves better fairness x accuracy trade-off than alternatives under adversarial missingness using worst-case fairness optimization.

papers.title: Fair-FedMOE: Group-Fair One-Shot Federated Learning via Prototype-Guided Experts for Medical Imaging Analysis
papers.contribution: Fair-FedMOE demonstrates consistent fairness gains without sacrificing accuracy on retinal and chest X-ray datasets with multiple foundation models.

papers.title: FairGB: A Fair Granular-Ball Generation Method for Data Classification
papers.contribution: Generates locally fair granular balls while preserving high purity, achieving superior trade-off between accuracy and fairness compared to state-of-the-art baselines while maintaining interpretability.

papers.title: FairMerging: Rethinking Model Merging through the Lens of Fairness
papers.contribution: FairMerging substantially mitigates unfairness while retaining competitive multi-task performance across multiple datasets, backbones, and merging baselines.

papers.title: FairRARI: A Plug and Play Framework for Fairness-Aware PageRank
papers.contribution: Achieve target fairness levels with same asymptotic time-complexity as original PageRank while maintaining utility.

papers.title: FairSSL: Fair Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning
papers.contribution: Significantly improves fairness on heterogeneous multimodal datasets without sacrificing downstream predictive performance.

papers.title: Fairness in Aggregation: Optimal Top-$k$ and Improved Full Ranking
papers.contribution: Makes significant progress on fair rank aggregation, closing computational gap between fair and unconstrained aggregation.

papers.title: Flattery, Fluff, and Fog: Diagnosing and Mitigating Idiosyncratic Biases in Preference Models
papers.contribution: CDA reduces average miscalibration from 39.4% to 32.5% across preference models.

papers.title: HoloFair: Unified T2I Fairness Evaluation and Fair-GRPO Debiasing
papers.contribution: Fair-GRPO significantly improves multidimensional fairness on SD3.5-Medium while maintaining high image quality with analysis of reward hacking mitigation.

papers.title: In Agents We Trust, but Who Do Agents Trust? Latent Preferences Steer LLM Generations
papers.contribution: Shows several models consistently exhibit strong predictable source preferences sensitive to context, outweighing content influence, explaining phenomena like left-leaning news recommendation bias.

papers.title: Incentivizing Truthfulness and Collaborative Fairness in Bayesian Learning
papers.contribution: First mechanism provably ensuring collaborative fairness and incentivizing truthfulness at equilibrium for Bayesian models, validated on synthetic and real-world datasets.

papers.title: Iterative Robust Satisficing: Minimizing Performance Degradation Under Distribution Shift
papers.contribution: Improves worst-case group performance without sacrificing overall accuracy with per-step cost similar to standard SGD, across synthetic and real distribution shifts.

papers.title: LLMS ON TRIAL: Evaluating Judicial Fairness For Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Experiments uncover pervasive inconsistency, bias, and imbalanced inaccuracy across models, revealing severe LLM judicial unfairness with pronounced biases on demographic labels.

papers.title: Locate then Correct: Debiasing Attention Heads in CLIP
papers.contribution: Achieves over 50% gain in worst-group accuracy on bias benchmarks compared to post-hoc baselines.

papers.title: Long-term Fairness with Selective Labels
papers.contribution: Proposes a reinforcement learning algorithm for long-term fair decision-making with selective labels, validated on semisynthetic hiring and lending scenarios.

papers.title: MAFE: Enabling Equitable Algorithm Design in Multi-Agent Multi-Stage Decision-Making Systems
papers.contribution: Enable reproducible evaluation of fairness-aware policies and reveal critical trade-offs between fairness, performance, and coordination through experiments on loan processing, healthcare, and education.

papers.title: Maximin Relative Improvement: Fair Learning as a Bargaining Problem
papers.contribution: Relative improvement provides axiomatic fairness justification and establishes finite-sample convergence guarantees under mild conditions.

papers.title: On Fairness of Task Arithmetic: The Role of Task Vectors
papers.contribution: Establishes task arithmetic as fairness-aware alternative with tunable subgroup-specific task vectors achieving competitive accuracy while reducing disparities.

papers.title: One Bias After Another: Mechanistic Reward Shaping and Persistent Biases in Language Reward Models
papers.contribution: Reduces targeted biases without degrading reward quality and generalizes out-of-distribution.

papers.title: Online Fair Division with Additional Information
papers.contribution: Provides learning-augmented algorithms with robust fairness guarantees that degrade gracefully under noisy information.

papers.title: Optimal Fair Aggregation of Crowdsourced Noisy Labels using Demographic Parity Constraints
papers.contribution: Derives upper bounds on fairness gap of Majority Vote and shows fairness gap converges exponentially to ground-truth under interpretable conditions, demonstrates post-processing effectiveness on synthetic and real datasets.

papers.title: Optimal Transport under Group Fairness Constraints
papers.contribution: Enables efficient computation of fair transport plans with theoretical guarantees and empirical validation of fairness-cost trade-offs.

papers.title: RECAST: Model Reconstruction via Counterfactual-Aware Wasserstein Geometry under Limited Data
papers.contribution: Achieves high surrogate fidelity in low-sample regimes with stable results under limited and noisy access, improving fairness diagnostics.

papers.title: Rethinking Pareto Frontier: On the Optimal Trade-offs in Fair Classification
papers.contribution: Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our method in achieving better fairness-accuracy trade-off, and that our MS Pareto frontiers suf

papers.title: Riemannian Optimization for Fair Spectral Clustering
papers.contribution: R-FairSC significantly improves computational efficiency over state-of-the-art methods while maintaining high clustering quality and fairness constraints.

papers.title: Test-Time Debiasing with Probabilistic Prompts via Wasserstein Distance in Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Improves robustness in multi-class debiasing with stronger fairness-utility trade-off across diverse VLM evaluations.

papers.title: WRING Out The Bias: A Rotation-Based Alternative To Projection Debiasing
papers.contribution: Rotation-based approach mitigates unintended bias amplification while debiasing known concepts in VLM embeddings.
